publications.title: The LEGO Group teams up with Sesame Street to inspire young children to fall in love with nature
publications.summary: Responsibility October 27, 2026 The LEGO Group teams up with Sesame Street to inspire young children to fall in love with nature The LEGO Group and Sesame Workshop, the global nonprofit behind Sesame Street, have launched three new videos, funded by the LEGO Foundation, encouraging children aged 4 to 6 to discover the natural world through play. Featuring Elmo, Cookie Monster and other Sesame Street friends, the videos introduce children to bats, butterflies and worms before inviting them to build habitats using LEGO bricks and everyday craft materials. The LEGO Group’s free activity guides and printables help families and educators extend the experience through hands-on play at home and in community settings.

publications.title: Ciao, Venice: The LEGO Group floats new Icons set

publications.title: Review: 72161 Drone Search for Mythical Mew
publications.summary: Long before Grogu, another cute, rare, powerful, and seemingly ageless creature was sought after for its special properties—in the hopes of engineering ultimate beings . With this set, you too can search for such a mythical marvel, but hopefully for some less nefarious purposes. Back in my day, Mew was a schoolyard legend, as finding it needed a glitchy miracle, and the process was not a simple internet search away! Now kids can just use a drone—and a surprisingly fun one at that! Please note, this set does not contain a SMART Brick. Continue reading » © 2026 Brickset.com . Republication prohibited without prior permission.

publications.title: Which is the best modular building?
publications.summary: The first phase of our quest to determine your favourite modular building is complete. Over 4,000 votes were cast in our poll which was used to whittle down 21 contenders to just eight. Those eight are as follows, grouped in seeded pairs for the quarter-finals of the knockout phase of the contest: 10255 Assembly Square 10251 Brick Bank 10297 Boutique Hotel 10350 Tudor Corner 10260 Downtown Diner 10246 Detective's Office 10326 Natural History Museum 10243 Parisian Restaurant The next stage will hopefully commence on Monday with the first two of the four quarter-final contests. But we need your help: we need people to advocate for them, to write a paragraph or two about why people should vote for their set rather than their competitor. If you'd like to do so, just drop a note in the comments stating which one you'd like to advocate for and I'll be in touch. I've listed the unsuccessful buildings and the number of votes they received after the break. I'm a little surprised that the latest one didn't get much love... Continue reading » © 2026 Brickset.com . Republication prohibited without prior permission.

publications.title: 21375 Godzilla, the biggest ever LEGO Ideas set, revealed!
publications.summary: Godzilla by MattE720 was selected for production on LEGO Ideas last summer and there has been huge excitement for the model since. It has finally been announced today, containing over 5000 pieces, which makes this the largest Ideas set ever! The press release follows: 21375 Godzilla Rated 18+, 5,363 pieces $449.99 / £349.99 / €399.99 Available at LEGO.com from 27th November Celebrate a legend of the Monsterverse and pop culture icon with this collectable LEGO Ideas Godzilla ( 21375 ) building set for adults 18 years and up. It’s an ideal gift for men, women and monster merch collectors. Immerse yourself in the rewarding challenge of capturing the Titan’s imposing presence and recreating his scaly skin and jagged dorsal fins. Inspired by a Fan Designer’s idea, voted for by fans and produced by the LEGO Group, this poseable Godzilla brick-built figure makes an epic piece of movie decor for any living room or office. Once built with its tail to the left or right, adjust its head, arms, wrists and fingers for fierce battle poses. Replace his tongue with the Heat Ray to fire up a display that is sure to spark nostalgic memories for generations of fans. Continue reading » © 2026 Brickset.com . publications.title: My LEGO 'Fear'
publications.summary: Happy Hallowe'en! There are many things to fear in LEGO sets, from expensive prices and poor colour matching to agonisingly descriptive set names and the recently-revealed 67012 The Joker Wall Art Comic Cover. However, I encountered something else I really dislike while constructing 75645 Battle at Drum Castle yesterday: the dreaded 'sticker applied on the inside of a wall panel'! These are occasionally a necessary feature, where space is at an absolute premium, but I find them annoying for a number of reasons. Chief among them is that I think such details can be brick-built in the vast majority of cases and that is certainly the case with the shelves in Drum Castle. Also, they are tricky stickers to apply because it can be easy to trap dust or air bubbles underneath and you only have one chance to place them, as you cannot reach the corners to lift them for another attempt, trapped inside the panel as they are. Even worse is the horrifying 'sticker applied on the inside of a curved wall panel', but those are fortunately quite rare nowadays. I still remember my apprehension placing a sticker on the inside of an 8x4x6 half cone element in 76387 Hogwarts: Fluffy Encounter! Do you have any LEGO fears like mine?
